voyage.content: The renamed Rome Zoo, one of the oldest in Europe, founded in 1911. On the edge of the Borghese Gardens, a short, well-signposted walk from the Gallery. They try hard, but San Diego this isn't. If you are a regular zoo-goer you will be disappointed.

voyage.name: Piazza del Popolo Obelisk
voyage.content: According to an inscription Emperor Augustus dedicated the obelisk to the sun in the 11th year of his consulate (10BC), after he had annexed Egypt to Rome. The obelisk is 24 m high. It was erected in Heliopolis in Egypt and was dedicated to Pharao Sethos I (1313-1292 BC) and Pharoa Ramses II (1292-1275 BC). Augustus brought the obelisk to the Circus Maximus, where it was rediscovered in 1587, broken into three pieces

voyage.name: Statue of Lord Byron
voyage.content: Statue by Thorvaldsen.

voyage.name: Auditorium Parco della Musica
voyage.content: The Auditorium at Parco della Musica is a large complex on the north side of Rome, built on a site that was part of the 1960 Olympic area. It is composed of three separate halls whose shapes are inspired by musical instruments. These are positioned around an open air amphitheatre, that is used nearly every night in the summer for concerts. The interiors are entirely made of cherry-wood, which provides for good acoust

voyage.name: Il Margutta RistorArte
voyage.content: A fairly decent vegetarian lunch buffet. The staff can point out the vegan eats. A decent value for the money. Near where Fellini once lived.

voyage.name: Fiaschetteria Beltramme da Cesaretto
voyage.hours: Open for lunch and dinner. Closed Sun
voyage.content: Outdoor seating available. Cash only. Walls lined with interesting art and at least one communal table. Small, traditional menu but the best dishes are the pastas and the simple bresaola, rughetta and parmigiano plate. Recommended dishes are the tonnarelli cacio & pepe and maltagliati al sugo.

voyage.name: La Casa del Cremolato
voyage.content: One of the best Cafe of the area. Try the homemade cremolato, probably one of the best in Rome.

voyage.name: Caffè Vaticano
voyage.content: Delicious fruit gelato with exotic fruit bits, ice creams and coffees.

voyage.name: Osteria delle Commari
voyage.content: An Italian restaurant that does not do pizza. A little expensive.

voyage.name: Siciliainbocca
voyage.price: Reasonable prices; fish plate around €15, but do order some antipasti and pasta
voyage.content: Nice Sicilian restaurant in the quiet (and somewhat boring) part of northern Prati. Try the swordfish and the lemon sorbet!

voyage.name: Babington's Tea Rooms
voyage.content: situated right next to the base of the Spanish Steps, a veritable tourist trap. The cheapest pot of tea is €8. It opened in 1896 in order to fortify homesick English tourists, once famous as a tranquil English haven in a Latin ocean, now serving tea and scones (and more) with considerably less charm and even less value.

voyage.name: Antico Caffe Greco
voyage.content: In March 2026, it is closed due to a rent dispute. Ancient and famous coffee bar, with walls lined with art work. Worth a quick look even if you find the prices a bit excessive.

voyage.name: Babette caffe-ristorante
voyage.content: Lovely lunch buffet. Everything fresh out of the kitchen. Much more expensive on weekends. Always best to reserve. A nice way to sample lots of different Italian foods without having to order an antipasti, primi, secondi, etc.

voyage.name: Franklin Feel The Sound Hotel
voyage.content: Hotel with a unique music theme. The décor is very modern and stylish. Staff was helpful friendly and polite, continental breakfast is varied and plentiful. The rooms are clean, funky and very comfortable.

voyage.name: Filomena e Francesca B&B
voyage.content: Bed and Breakfast. Three rooms with private bathrooms and air-con.

voyage.name: Mocenigo Vatican Suites
voyage.content: Seven-room guesthouse 100 m from the main entrance to the Vatican Museums.

voyage.name: LH Excel Roma Montemario
voyage.address: via degli Scolopi 31, Montemario Area, zona Trionfale
voyage.content: This hotel has open air pool, restaurant, free parking and fitness center.

voyage.name: Hotel Cinquantatre
voyage.content: Hotel is in an old building with a roof-top terrace, rooms are with satellite TV, A/C and a safe, some with balcony as well.

voyage.name: Hotel Condotti
voyage.price: Single rooms from €136, double rooms from €175, triple rooms from €209, quadruple rooms from €223

voyage.name: Hotel Concordia
voyage.content: A hotel in an 18th-century building with A/C and a roof garden.

voyage.name: Imperial Suite Rome
voyage.price: €80/€95 single/double rooms. All rates include the breakfast served directly in the guests’ rooms
voyage.content: A guest house with single, double, twin and triple bedrooms. All with private bath, internet connection and living area.

voyage.name: PapavistaRelais
voyage.content: Guesthouse fairly close to the Vatican's main entrance.

voyage.name: Les Fleurs Luxury House
voyage.content: Cosy guest house with double and twin standard bedrooms €260, double deluxe, junior suite €380 and double for single use €230. All rates include breakfast and en-suites services with shower and bathtub or Jacuzzi.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn Rome Claridge
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in the Parioli district, close to the Borghese Gardens.

voyage.name: Hotel Lord Byron
voyage.price: single rooms from €190, double rooms from €225

voyage.name: B&B Domus Pinciana
voyage.content: Small B&B close to Via Veneto.

voyage.name: Intown Luxury House
voyage.content: Single, double, junior suite and terraced junior suite. All rooms with A/C, LCD TV sets with satellite channels, hi-speed Internet connection, safe, minibar and direct telephone line. Bathrooms are fitted with marble and Jacuzzi tubs and/or showers.

voyage.name: Best Western Astrid
voyage.content: A big hotel in a quiet area of Rome. The staff is friendly and makes the stay very enjoyable. The rooms are clean and spacious and there’s a daily replenishment of the minibar at no cost. The 5th-floor breakfast room has great views of the Tiber and St. Peter's Dome. The bar is closed at night and there isn't much nightlife in the area apart from a few good restaurants.

voyage.name: Spagna Royal Suite Rome
voyage.content: Boutique hotel. Double, triple and quadruple rooms divided in standard, comfort, deluxe and executive. All with private bath. Rates change according to the season, starting from £239 for a double standard and €399 for a triple deluxe.

voyage.name: Town House Spagna
voyage.content: Relatively new town house 50 m away from Piazza di Spagna. 10 rooms, each with private bathrooms. Up to date facilities.

voyage.name: c-hotels Fiume Roma
voyage.content: Nice hotel near the Villa Borghese park.

voyage.name: New Homs
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Stendhal
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Hotel Spring House
voyage.content: A small 3-star hotel with rooms that are a bit small, but comfortable and quiet. Great breakfast, wonderful service (maids and reception).

voyage.name: Hotel Museum Rome
voyage.content: Nice three-star hotel, 35 bedrooms with air conditioning and free Wi-Fi, large common area, complimentary breakfast, and terrace with panoramic view of the Roman roofs.

voyage.name: San Crisogono
voyage.content: Underneath the beautiful baroque church (with repurposed ancient Roman columns) there is a surprisingly large crypt, where ancient Roman ruins can be viewed. You can also see beautiful early Christian frescoes. Entry is €3 per person, payable in cash only.

voyage.name: Casa della Fornarina
voyage.content: There is little information available on Raphael's mistress La Fornarina. Margherita was the daughter of a baker from Siena. His shop was near Villa Farnesina where Raphael was painting. It is reported that Raphael repudiated her on his death bed as he wanted to be redeemed from his sins. Four months after his death Margherita joined the monastery Santa Apollonia in Trastevere. It is said that she was model for Rapha

voyage.name: Ponte Sisto
voyage.content: Pope Sixtus IV della Rovere (1471-1481) gave order to replace the old Roman bridge by a new one. It was Pope Sixtus IV who also ordered the Sistine Chapel and the Opsedale di Santo Spirito to be built. So he ran out of money. He levied a tax on prostitution in order to gain money for the construction of the Ponte Sisto.

voyage.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
voyage.content: One of the oldest churches in the city. The nave is lined with a mismatched collection of columns taken from ancient Roman buildings. The apse is covered in gold mosaics from the 13th century, arguably the finest mosaics in the city. Impressive mosaics also on the front. According to legend the church was founded in 222, so it would be one of the most ancient churches in the city. Written records mention a church on

voyage.name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
voyage.address: Piazza di Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
voyage.content: Very ornately done and beautiful inside, but don't expect any information in English. All information panels are only in Italian. It's still a beautiful site though even if you don't read Italian. According to tradition St.Cecily suffered a particular cruel death as a martyr. She was scalded, suffocated and beheaded by three strokes on her neck. As she was singing all the time during her martyrdom she is considered t

voyage.name: San Francesco a Ripa
voyage.hours: open to the public every day from 08:00 to 13:00 and from 14:00 to 19:30. During the liturgical celebrations is not possible to visit the church or the shrine
voyage.content: Named after St. Francis of Assisi, who stayed nearby. Inside the Paluzzi-Albertoni chapel is one of Bernini’s masterpieces, the statue of the Blessed Ludovica Albertoni. The column in front of the church comes from the ruins of Veii (see Rome/North).

voyage.name: Villa Farnesina
voyage.content: Delightful Renaissance house that was built by a rich banker from Siena, Agostino Chigi. In 1577 it was bought by the Farnese family and has since been known as Villa Farnesina. At one time there were plans by Michelangelo to build a bridge over the river to connect the villa with Palazzo Farnese on the other side. You can tour several beautiful rooms that are all decorated with frescoes, including some by Raphael. P

voyage.name: National Gallery of Ancient Art
voyage.content: housed in the baroque palace Corsini where Christina, Queen of Sweden settled down in the last years of her life

voyage.name: Orto Botanico dell'Università di Roma "La Sapienza"
voyage.content: This garden was established in 1883. It has over 3,500 species of plants and includes a "Scent-and-Touch" garden for those who are visually impaired.

voyage.name: Museum of Rome in Trastevere
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-20:00, Mon closed. Last admission 1h before closing
voyage.content: Permanent collection features paintings and drawings of Rome between the 18th and 20th centuries together with a fascinating black and white photo exhibition of Rome from 1950-80. Also offers rotating exhibitions, usually of the work of photographers.

voyage.name: Villa Sciarra
voyage.content: A lovely, if somewhat run-down park (parts of it are blocked due to the poor state of the roads) with statues and a great view on the city.

voyage.name: Il Gianicolo
voyage.content: This is not, contrary to popular belief, one of the original seven hills that Rome was founded on. It is the second highest after Monte Mario, though, and offers incredible panoramic views of the city as long as the authorities remember to prune the trees on the hillside (if they are too tall you can walk a few meters down the hill for views that are just as good). On the other side of the piazza there is also a nice

voyage.name: San Pietro in Montorio
voyage.content: This church, which was commissioned by Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain, marks the point where, according to tradition, St. Peter was crucified. Particularly interesting for Irish visitors as it contains the graves of three Gaelic Chiefs who fled Ireland in 1607.

voyage.name: The Tempietto
voyage.content: Designed by Bramante to mark the spot of St. Peter's martyrdom, this delightful miniature building is considered a masterpiece of Renaissance architecture. Open to the public.

voyage.name: Fontana dell'Acqua Paola
voyage.content: This massive early 17th-century Baroque fountain was built to celebrate the re-opening of an old Roman aqueduct. Water played an important role in this area in Roman times as the grain was milled here using water mills.

voyage.name: Manfredi Lighthouse
voyage.content: Strange to see a lighthouse on top of a hill. This was built in 1911 and was a gift to the city from Italians living in Argentina. From here you can continue down the hill, past Rome's largest and Italy's most important children's hospital, Bambino Gesu, eventually arriving at the River Tiber close to the Vatican.

voyage.name: Get lost in Trastevere
voyage.content: The cobbled streets are narrow and winding and random but losing your way will lead you to places you might not otherwise find. Note that the cobblestone streets (locally called sampietrini) are being paved elsewhere in Rome as the vibrations from cars driving over them have been found to lead to cracking in the foundations of many of the monuments and historic sites around the city. The sampietrini are mostly being

voyage.name: Piazza S. Maria in Trastevere
voyage.content: Beautiful place to hang around and watch people going by, as well as the many buskers usually found in the square. Join the students sitting on the steps of the fountain or, if you can afford it, have a drink or meal at one of the restaurants and bars on two sides of the square.

voyage.name: Big Mama
voyage.hours: Shows normally begin around 22:00 but check Press for details
voyage.address: Vicolo di San Francesco a Ripa 18
voyage.content: Rome’s original "House of the Blues". Has been going strong for 25 years. Italian and international artists, with blues and jazz concerts.

voyage.name: Porta Portese
voyage.content: On Sunday mornings there is a huge flea market. It extends from Porta Portese to Viale di Trastevere.

voyage.name: Ai Bozzi
voyage.content: Italian restaurant with excellent food and professional service. Traditional dishes as well innovative variations (try the fettuccine with artichokes and guanciale). Pizza is also served in the evening. Lovely outside terrace overlooking the piazza.

voyage.name: Augusto
voyage.content: A small osteria in the heart of Trastevere. Authentic non-touristic Roman restaurant serving classic Roman dishes, hand-made desserts and wine. It's a good idea to phone ahead to see if they have room because this small place fills up fast every night, although if you don't mind waiting they'll squeeze you in if they can. They do not take reservations.

voyage.name: Fior di luna
voyage.content: Very good ice cream and made from fair trade products by an ice cream artist with a passion for taste.

voyage.name: Glass Hostaria
voyage.content: Uber-modern trattoria.

voyage.name: Ivo a Trastevere
voyage.address: Via di S. Francesco a Ripa 158
voyage.content: Get here early if you want a table without a wait. Very popular pizzeria that attracts lengthy queues of young Romans, so it must be good.

voyage.name: La Gattabuia
voyage.content: Serves pizza, pasta and steak. Great atmosphere and friendly staff. Unique location and décor.

voyage.name: Osteria dell'Aquila
voyage.content: Mediterranean style restaurant. Menu is in Italian and English, and the waiters speak both languages. Open for lunch and dinner. The meals here are excellent and at very good prices. Make sure to try the seafood appetizers.

voyage.name: Osteria der Belli
voyage.content: Run by four brothers from Sardinia. Particularly recommended for its seafood dishes.

voyage.name: Pizzeria La Boccaccia
voyage.address: Via di San Francesco a Ripa 21
voyage.content: Great little pizzeria run by 2 friendly Neapolitan brothers. You can get a big slice and a huge ice cold beer for €5. The place gets full of locals. That should tell you everything. get there quite early as in the evening they have a few pizzas left, most popular time is around lunch and after school. Also note that the street Via di San Francesco a Ripa has a strange numbering system - odd and even numbers are on th

voyage.name: Il Vicola Da Tony
voyage.content: On a beautiful old Roman laneway with indoor and outdoor seating. One of the best lasagne in the city as well as plenty of pasta, meat and seafood options. Risotto alla pescatora (seafood risotto) is delicious; don't ask for the fish if you can't get a quick mortgage to pay for it. Prices bear no relation whatsoever to the menu.

voyage.name: Trattoria de Gli Amici
voyage.content: Very interesting place in the heart of Trastevere district. Run by very kind handicapped people, it has nice cuisine.

voyage.name: Vincenzo alla Lungaretta
voyage.content: Out of the way. Great food and great service and a very reasonable price.

voyage.name: Vivi Bistrot
voyage.content: Suitable for children as well. Useful for arranging a picnic in the park.

voyage.name: Enoteca Ferrara
voyage.content: Luxury restaurant

voyage.name: Sora Lella
voyage.hours: closed Sun, Tue morning and 2 weeks in August

voyage.name: Baccanale
voyage.content: A small bar with a great range of drinks, friendly staff and a manic display of cocktail making later on in the evening. There are several TV screens showing major sporting events. Probably the best bar in the world considering its location and stereotypical perfection. The staff are very welcoming to tourists. It is a secret that you'll be lucky to find in the narrow, winding streets of Trastevere.

voyage.name: Hotel Cisterna Rome
voyage.content: 2-star hotel with 24-hr reception. 20 rooms, All equipped with modern services and private bathrooms. Bookable online.

voyage.name: Roma Trasteverina B&B
voyage.price: Single €40-60, double €80-120, twin and double rooms

voyage.name: Relais Rome Sweet Home Trastevere
voyage.content: Small hotel with 4 rooms. All equipped with satTV, Wi-Fi and private bathrooms. Online booking.

voyage.name: Arco dei Tolomei
voyage.content: All the rooms come with private bath and shower.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Gianicolo Rome
voyage.content: Four star accommodation with twin, double with jacuzzi, triple and dus (double for single use). All with private bath and shower. Swimming pool, a private garden and a fantastic panoramic view of Rome.

voyage.name: Hotel Santa Maria
voyage.content: Gated hotel just off Piazza Santa Maria. Comfortable and has a nice courtyard.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa della Fonte
voyage.content: Small hotel, all rooms have a private bath, free Wi-Fi, satelliteTV and A/C.

voyage.name: WRH Trastevere
voyage.content: Friendly modern & minimalist guesthouse.

voyage.name: Gran Meliá Rome
voyage.content: A luxury 5-star hotel with single, double, triple and quadruple rooms, very quiet with a view of Vatican City.
